claims.text: Tailored thermomechanical processing can preserve and refine a lamellar eutectic microstructure into an ultrafine-grained duplex structure.
The resulting ultrafine-grained duplex structure improves the combination of strength and ductility relative to conventional processing.
The resulting ultrafine-grained duplex structure improves Young's modulus.
The resulting ultrafine-grained duplex structure improves fracture resistance.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy suitable for the proposed processing strategy.
The relevant as-cast starting state has a coarse lamellar or homogeneous microstructure.
Controlled rolling followed by annealing can inherit and refine the as-cast lamellar structure.
The method requires retention of the original lamellar morphology without excessive coarsening.
Avoiding loss of phase coherence is necessary for the method to work.
The processed material will contain an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure with hierarchical lamellar organization and phase-decomposition features.
The hierarchical lamellar and phase-decomposition features act as built-in reinforcements.
The refined architecture creates a two-hierarchical constraint effect that strengthens the alloy.
The refined architecture promotes a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism.
Microcrack arrest enhances macroscopic fracture resistance.
The hierarchical phase distribution can raise effective Young's modulus while maintaining ductility.
The processed samples should exhibit greater than 20% strain to failure.
The intervention is expected to increase strength by approximately 20–30% relative to conventional processing.
The intervention is expected to produce measurable gains in fracture toughness.
The approach may not work in non-eutectic HEAs or alloys prone to rapid grain coarsening.
Failure to form the refined duplex lamellar architecture or to improve all four target mechanical properties relative to a same-composition control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis says ductility will improve, whereas the predicted outcome allows ductility merely to be maintained; the falsification rule appears to require statistically significant improvement in ductility along with the other properties.
The initial state permits a homogeneous microstructure, but the intervention and stated applicability require an existing lamellar morphology to be inherited and refined.
